findings.title: Command Injection via Unsanitized repo_url in Git Clone
findings.description: In forge/app.py, the _resolve_repo_path function passes the user-supplied repo_url directly to subprocess.run for git clone without validating the URL scheme, format, or content. While shell=False prevents direct shell injection, git itself can interpret certain URL formats (e.g., git://host/repo, file:///etc/passwd, ext::command) in dangerous ways. The workspace name derived from the URL via regex is also used unsanitized as a directory path component. Multiple workers flagged this with high agreement.

locations.snippet:
match = re.search(r"/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$", repo_url.rstrip("/"))
name = match.group(1) if match else "repo"
workspace = os.path.join(WORKSPACES_DIR, name)
...
subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace], check=True, ...)

findings.suggested_fix: 1) Validate repo_url with urlparse: only allow https:// scheme. 2) Validate hostname against an allowlist or at minimum reject file://, git://, ext::, and other dangerous schemes. 3) Sanitize the extracted repo name to only allow alphanumeric, hyphens, and underscores. 4) Verify the constructed workspace path is within WORKSPACES_DIR using Path.resolve().

findings.title: Path Traversal in Context Builder File Operations
findings.description: forge/execution/context_builder.py reads arbitrary file paths from the codebase_map without validating that they resolve within the repository root. An attacker who can influence codebase_map content (e.g., via a malicious checkpoint or crafted repo) could inject paths like ../../etc/passwd to read arbitrary files. Two waves of security workers independently flagged this with consistent severity assessment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a repo_root parameter to read_file_safe. Before reading: resolved = Path(path).resolve(); if not resolved.is_relative_to(Path(repo_root).resolve()): raise ValueError('Path traversal detected'). Apply this check in select_files_for_pass and build_codebase_inventory.

findings.title: Path Traversal in Checkpoint File Operations
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py constructs checkpoint file paths using os.path.join(repo_path, CHECKPOINT_DIR) without validating that repo_path doesn't contain traversal sequences. A malicious repo_path like /real/repo/../../etc could write checkpoint files outside the intended directory. Additionally, clear_checkpoints uses shutil.rmtree without validating the target is within expected bounds, potentially enabling symlink attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: In _checkpoint_path: resolve both repo_path and cp_dir with Path.resolve() and verify cp_dir.is_relative_to(resolved_repo). For clear_checkpoints: verify cp_dir is within expected bounds before rmtree, and check for symlinks with os.path.islink before following.

findings.title: Insecure Checkpoint Deserialization Without Integrity Verification
findings.description: Checkpoint files in .forge-checkpoints/ are loaded and deserialized without any integrity verification (no HMAC, no signature). An attacker with write access to the checkpoint directory can tamper with files to inject malicious data that gets reconstructed into CodebaseMap, AuditFinding, and other Pydantic models. While Pydantic validates types, it doesn't prevent injection of semantically malicious values (e.g., crafted file paths, finding IDs). Multiple workers flagged this consistently.

locations.snippet:
with open(path, "r") as f:
    data = json.load(f)
cp = ForgeCheckpoint(**data)

state.codebase_map = CodebaseMap(**cp.codebase_map)
state.security_findings = [AuditFinding(**f) for f in cp.security_findings]

findings.suggested_fix: Add HMAC-SHA256 signature to checkpoint files using a run-specific secret. Store signature alongside data and verify before deserializing. Alternatively, store checkpoints in a location only writable by the forge process. Also add validation of restored repo_path against current repo_path.

findings.title: God Module: forge/app.py Violates Single Responsibility
findings.description: forge/app.py is a monolithic orchestrator (~245 lines) handling: platform detection, conditional AgentField import, repo cloning, workspace management, telemetry lifecycle, checkpoint recovery, pipeline phase orchestration (discovery/triage/remediation/validation), worktree cleanup, and result construction. This was flagged by both architecture and quality workers in both waves with very high confidence. It makes the module untestable, unmaintainable, and a merge conflict hotspot.

locations.snippet: async def remediate(...) -> dict: # ~150 lines handling all pipeline phases

findings.suggested_fix: Extract into focused modules: forge/execution/repo_resolver.py (clone/path logic), forge/execution/pipeline.py (phase orchestration), forge/execution/telemetry_context.py (telemetry lifecycle wrapper). The remediate() function should delegate to these, becoming ~30 lines.

findings.title: Unhandled CalledProcessError from Git Clone Subprocess
findings.description: forge/app.py calls subprocess.run with check=True for git clone but has no try/except around it. A network failure, invalid URL, or authentication error causes an unhandled CalledProcessError to propagate up through remediate(), bypassing telemetry cleanup and worktree cleanup in the finally block (since the exception occurs before try). Two quality workers flagged this in both waves.

locations.snippet:
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace],
    check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
)

findings.suggested_fix: Wrap subprocess.run in try/except subprocess.CalledProcessError and raise a user-friendly ForgeCloneError with the stderr output. Also move subprocess and re imports to module level.

findings.title: Silent Checkpoint Failures Risk Data Loss
findings.description: Both save_checkpoint and load_checkpoint catch all exceptions and log them without propagating. A checkpoint save failure during a long remediation run results in silent data loss—the user sees no error and believes progress is saved, but resume will restart from the beginning. Multiple workers flagged this in both waves.

locations.snippet:
except Exception as e:
    logger.error("Failed to save checkpoint for %s: %s", phase.value, e)

findings.suggested_fix: Add a ForgeConfig option checkpoint_failure_mode: Literal['strict', 'lenient'] = 'lenient'. In strict mode, re-raise the exception. Always log at ERROR level. For load failures, add a specific warning that a fresh run will start. For save failures in strict mode, halt the pipeline.

findings.title: File Descriptor Leak in build_codebase_inventory
findings.description: forge/execution/context_builder.py opens files with fpath.open() inside a loop without using a context manager. While CPython's reference counting typically closes files promptly, this is not guaranteed and can cause file descriptor exhaustion on large repositories or with alternative Python implementations. Two quality workers flagged this in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: `with fpath.open(errors='replace') as f: loc = sum(1 for _ in f)`

findings.title: Duplicated File Selection Logic in context_builder.py
findings.description: select_files_for_pass and select_files_for_quality_pass in context_builder.py contain nearly identical logic for file reading, token budget management, and content assembly. Only the scoring keyword sets differ. This violates DRY and means bug fixes or improvements must be applied twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract common logic into _select_files_impl(repo_path, scored_files, token_budget) -> str. Both public functions score files differently then call the shared impl.

findings.title: Telemetry Context Manager Misuse — Manual __enter__/__exit__ Calls
findings.description: forge/app.py manually calls _telemetry_ctx.__enter__() and later _telemetry_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None) instead of using async with or contextlib. The None arguments to __exit__ don't propagate exception information correctly. If an exception occurs before the try block but after __enter__, cleanup is skipped. Two quality workers flagged this in both waves.

locations.snippet:
if _telemetry_ctx is not None:
    _telemetry_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)

findings.suggested_fix: Refactor remediate() to use `async with telemetry.activate():` if the context manager supports it, or use contextlib.AsyncExitStack to manage multiple context managers. This is part of the broader app.py refactor (F-005).

findings.title: Unvalidated FORGE_PORT Environment Variable Causes Crash
findings.description: forge/__main__.py calls int(os.getenv('FORGE_PORT', '8004')) without try/except. A misconfigured environment (e.g., FORGE_PORT=disabled) raises an unhandled ValueError at startup. Flagged by both security and quality workers.

findings.title: Missing JSON Error Handling in CLI Report Command
findings.description: forge/cli.py reads and parses a report JSON file with json.loads() without catching JSONDecodeError. A corrupted or partially written report file causes an unhandled crash instead of a user-friendly error message.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap in try/except json.JSONDecodeError and emit a user-friendly error via typer.echo.

findings.title: Conditional Import Pattern Creates Fragile Platform Detection
findings.description: forge/app.py uses try/except ImportError to conditionally import AgentField and sets app=None if unavailable. This implicit mode switching makes it hard to reason about which features are active, and function-level imports scattered through remediate() further obscure dependencies. Flagged by architecture workers in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Create an explicit PlatformMode enum. Create separate entry modules forge/platform_app.py and forge/standalone.py. Move function-level imports to module level. The mode should be determined once at startup and injected consistently.

findings.title: Circular Import Risk via Function-Level Lazy Imports
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py imports forge.schemas inside restore_state() at function call time. This hides a potential circular dependency—if schemas ever imports from checkpoint (directly or transitively), the code breaks at runtime. ARCH-004 and ARCH-009 both flagged this pattern across modules.
findings.suggested_fix: Move imports to module top-level. Use TYPE_CHECKING guard for type-only annotations to break any actual circular dependency: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from forge.schemas import ForgeExecutionState`

findings.title: Missing Type Annotation on restore_state Return Value
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py declares restore_state() -> Any despite always returning ForgeExecutionState. This loses static type safety for all callers and makes the API contract unclear.
findings.suggested_fix: Change return type to ForgeExecutionState (using TYPE_CHECKING import if needed to avoid circular imports).

findings.title: Configuration Scattered Across Multiple Modules
findings.description: Magic numbers and configuration values are defined in multiple places: CHARS_PER_TOKEN=4 and DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET=80_000 in context_builder.py, WORKSPACES_DIR in app.py, max retries hardcoded in forge_executor.py. There is no single authoritative configuration surface. Flagged by multiple architecture workers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add token_budget, chars_per_token, workspaces_dir, max_inner_retries fields to ForgeConfig in config.py. Reference ForgeConfig in all modules that currently have magic numbers.

findings.title: Inconsistent Error Handling in asyncio.gather Calls
findings.description: forge/execution/forge_executor.py uses asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True and substitutes default empty results for agent failures. This means a test generator or code reviewer failure silently produces an empty/default result rather than clearly failing the fix attempt. The behavior is intentional but undocumented and potentially masks real failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Document explicitly why silent default results are acceptable (or not). Add a metric counter for agent failures. Consider adding a max_agent_failures threshold in ForgeConfig that triggers a fix failure rather than silent default.

findings.title: Checkpoint Resume Validation Missing Repo Path Check
findings.description: forge/app.py resumes from checkpoint based only on forge_run_id without validating that the checkpoint's repo_path matches the current run's repo_path. Running FORGE on repo B after a failed run on repo A in the same workspace could result in applying repo A's state to repo B.
findings.suggested_fix: Add validation: if cp.repo_path != resolved_repo_path: logger.warning('Checkpoint repo_path mismatch, ignoring checkpoint'); cp = None. Also validate forge_run_id format.

findings.title: Hardcoded Role Strings Duplicated Across Config Dicts
findings.description: Role name strings like 'codebase_analyst', 'security_auditor', etc. appear in FORGE_ROLE_TO_MODEL_FIELD, FORGE_DEFAULT_MODELS, and ROLE_TO_PROVIDER dictionaries in config.py, plus referenced in other files. A role rename requires updating multiple locations.

locations.snippet:
FORGE_ROLE_TO_MODEL_FIELD: dict[str, str] = {"codebase_analyst": ..., ...}
ROLE_TO_PROVIDER: dict[str, str] = {"codebase_analyst": ..., ...}

findings.suggested_fix: Define an AgentRole enum (or StrEnum in Python 3.11+) with all role names. Use it as keys in all dicts. This provides IDE support and prevents typos.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on LLM API Calls
findings.description: The FORGE system invokes multiple LLM agents concurrently (enabled by enable_parallel_audit=True) without any rate limiting, backoff, or circuit breaker. This can cause API quota exhaustion, unexpected cost spikes, or provider-side throttling that manifests as opaque errors. Flagged by both security workers in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Add max_concurrent_invocations and max_requests_per_minute to ForgeConfig. Implement a semaphore-based concurrency limiter in forge_executor.py. Add exponential backoff for rate limit (429) responses.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Potentially Exposed in Logs and Telemetry
findings.description: The telemetry system logs full finding descriptions, summaries, and file changes (which may contain extracted secrets or sensitive code) via log_training_pair. Additionally, AGENTFIELD_API_KEY is passed to the Agent constructor and could be captured by debug loggers. Flagged by security workers in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: 1) Add a logging.Filter that redacts values matching API key patterns. 2) Add a sanitize_for_telemetry() function that strips potential secrets from finding descriptions before logging. 3) Document that telemetry files should not be committed.

findings.title: sys.modules Manipulation in Integration Test Conftest is Fragile
findings.description: tests/integration/conftest.py directly manipulates sys.modules to inject a mock agentfield module. This is a global side effect that couples test execution order to import order, can cause intermittent failures, and makes it impossible to run individual integration tests in isolation. Flagged by both architecture and quality workers in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Use pytest's monkeypatch fixture scoped to session, or use unittest.mock.patch as a decorator on tests that need the mock. If module-level mocking is unavoidable (due to import-time side effects), document clearly and add a comment explaining why.

findings.title: Parallel Test File Writes to Shared Benchmark Log Without Locking
findings.description: tests/integration/conftest.py appends to .forge-benchmarks/cost_log.jsonl from multiple test processes without file locking. Parallel test runs (e.g., pytest-xdist) can corrupt this file.
findings.suggested_fix: Use fcntl.flock for POSIX or a threading.Lock for single-process parallelism. Alternatively, write per-worker files (e.g., cost_log_worker{id}.jsonl) and merge in a final step.

findings.title: Test Helper Functions Duplicated Across Test Files
findings.description: _copy_golden in test_golden_suite.py and _copy_golden_codebase in test_hive_live_e2e.py serve the same purpose with slightly different signatures. Mock response builders (_coder_ok, _test_ok, _review_ok) could leverage conftest factories. DRY violation increases maintenance burden.
findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single copy_golden(name, dest_dir) function in tests/conftest.py or tests/fixtures/helpers.py. Add assertion that source directory exists before copying.

findings.title: Hardcoded /tmp Paths in Test State Helpers
findings.description: tests/integration/test_execute_remediation.py hardcodes /tmp/test-repo and /tmp/test-artifacts as paths in ForgeExecutionState. These can conflict between parallel test runs and may not be writable on all systems.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert _state_with_plan() to a @pytest.fixture that uses the tmp_path fixture for isolated, system-appropriate temp directories.

findings.title: Fragile String-Based Reasoner Dispatch in Tests
findings.description: tests/integration/test_execute_remediation.py uses substring matching ('run_coder' in reasoner) to route mock responses. If production reasoner names change, tests silently return empty dicts rather than failing loudly.
findings.suggested_fix: Import reasoner name constants from production code (or a shared constants module) rather than using magic strings. Add a final else branch that raises ValueError for unrecognized reasoners.

findings.title: Golden Codebases Contain Real Vulnerabilities — Risk of Misuse
findings.description: tests/golden/codebases/ contains SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, and missing auth — intentionally for testing but without clear documentation. These could be accidentally packaged into distributions or used as templates. Multiple workers flagged this (as info/low in tests context).
findings.suggested_fix: 1) Add a README.md in tests/golden/codebases/ explaining these are intentionally vulnerable test fixtures. 2) Add a .gitignore entry or setup.cfg exclude to prevent packaging. 3) Add a top-of-file comment in each file: '# INTENTIONALLY INSECURE - test fixture only'.

findings.title: Inconsistent Async Test Marker Usage
findings.description: Some async tests explicitly use @pytest.mark.asyncio while others rely on auto-detection. This can cause tests to be silently skipped in strict mode configurations.
findings.suggested_fix: Set asyncio_mode = 'auto' in pytest.ini or pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] to normalize behavior, then remove redundant explicit markers.

findings.title: resolved_models() Dict Created on Every Call — Performance
findings.description: forge/config.py ForgeConfig.resolved_models() creates a new dictionary on every call by copying FORGE_DEFAULT_MODELS and applying overrides. model_for_role() calls resolved_models() internally. This is called in tight executor loops.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the result using @functools.cached_property or a private _resolved_models field initialized in model_post_init().

findings.title: Test conftest.py Combines Too Many Responsibilities
findings.description: tests/conftest.py (~200 lines) combines schema factories, pytest hooks (pytest_addoption, pytest_configure, pytest_collection_modifyitems), and fixtures. This makes it hard to navigate and maintain.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into: tests/conftest.py (fixtures only), tests/pytest_plugins.py (hooks), tests/fixtures/factories.py (factory functions). Keep tests/fixtures/schemas.py as re-export.

Valid port values in range 1-65535 work correctly

items.title: Add JSON error handling in CLI report command

items.title: Fix return type annotation on restore_state

Path.resolve() used to canonicalize path before reading
ValueError raised if resolved path is not relative to repo_root
select_files_for_pass and build_codebase_inventory pass repo_root to read_file_safe

Symlink check added before following paths in clear_checkpoints

load_checkpoint verifies signature before deserializing
Signature key is derived from forge_run_id or a configurable secret

remediation_plan.summary: 30 findings across security, quality, architecture, reliability, and performance categories. Execution is ordered in 7 levels: Level 1 applies 7 trivial deterministic fixes (Tier 1). Level 2 addresses the two critical security vulnerabilities (path traversal, command injection) plus related quality improvements in parallel. Level 3 applies dependent security fixes (integrity verification, error handling) and code deduplication. Levels 4-7 tackle architectural refactors that are interdependent: app.py decomposition (F-005) is the keystone enabling platform mode refactor (F-013) and config consolidation (F-016), which in turn enables rate limiting (F-020). Critical security findings F-001 through F-004 are highest priority as they represent exploitable attack surface. The golden codebase vulnerabilities (SEC-001 through SEC-011 in tests/) are intentional test fixtures and treated as documentation tasks rather than security remediations.

codebase_map.architecture_summary: FORGE is a Python-based LLM orchestration framework for automated code remediation. It follows a pipeline pattern: Discovery -> Triage -> Remediation -> Validation. The main entry points are a CLI (typer-based) and an AgentField agent. The execution engine uses checkpointing for resume capability, git worktrees for isolated fixes, and multiple specialized LLM agents for different roles. Configuration is partially centralized in ForgeConfig (Pydantic model) but scattered with magic numbers elsewhere. The codebase has a monolithic app.py orchestrator that needs decomposition. Tests include golden codebases with intentional vulnerabilities for detection testing.
